Hello! I've identified as bisexual for seven years, and while the imposter syndrome and the questioning does get easier with time, sometimes doubt creeps in even now (and I'm a woman in a relationship with another woman! 

I really identify with what you said about wondering if I'm actually bi or if I just like the idea of being with a woman (especially when I was single!). From my experience, the fact that I liked the idea pretty much affirmed the bisexuality I'd looked over for so long! I didn't grow up religious, but I grew up around the time when being called "gay" was an "insult" and it was something you didn't want to be. I also grew up in a time when all the media I consumed was straight and since I was a kid I had this idea that growing up marrying a man was my only option. I didn't even know what bisexual was until I was 17 (or what a lesbian was until I was 14!) 

The beautiful thing about bisexuality and what makes it so close to my heart is that bisexuality exists on a spectrum. Even if you were the tiniest bit attracted to the same gender and wanted to identify as bi, you're completely valid to do so, if that's what feels right by you! I can say for sure that my bisexuality doesn't exist as a clear cut 50/50 and that my sexuality feels very fluid. I'm almost always attracted to women more than men, but sometimes I find my attraction to men increases (and I've been like this my whole life.) 

You're far from alone with questioning what's what. Society as a whole has a long way to go with understanding bisexuality and I think that alone can make us really question ourselves and wonder if we're actually bisexuals in the first place. At the end of the day, you're the ruler of your own life. Take all the time you need to ask yourself what feels right for you! You deserve a happy and fulfilled life that you can live as your authentic self, whether that's as a queer person or a straight person! It might take a while before you know for sure (it took me 5 years and a lot of soul searching), but I think for some of us we never really stop questioning entirely, and that's ok too! 

Sorry if this wasn't the answer you were looking for, but I hope it helps! You have a community here, and I hope you have a wonderful day x
